names.name: The pink box
names.said: "Good things come in pink boxes" is a slogan somebody else wrote about somebody else's box.

text.what: The matte pink paperboard box a dozen donuts go into: the most recognisable object in the American trade, and the cheapest.
text.story:
The pink boxes that Southern California shops pack donuts in are attributed to Ted Ngoy and Ning Yen, who were setting other Cambodian families up in shops. Pink stock was cheaper than the glossy white box the trade used.

It travelled. Kenneth Pogson of Voodoo Doughnut adopted the box, and the slogan "Good things come in pink boxes", after a trip to California where he saw the boxes in use.
text.today: A pink box in a film or on a desk signals donuts without a logo, which is a thing very few products manage.

kin.as: The style named for it here.
